title: Senior Executive Restrictive Covenants Flagged Inadequate
rationale: Inadequate post-exit restrictive covenants on senior executives create meaningful risk to the 'backable management' thesis pillar and M&A pipeline continuity, warranting a condition to close requiring enhanced covenants, but does not independently threaten the base-case IRR absent evidence of imminent departure or competitor solicitation.
driver: Backable management / M&A industrialisation

title: Unregistered Trade Marks and IP Assignment Gaps (Courts Design)
rationale: Unregistered trade marks and IP assignment gaps in Courts Design create title risk over branding/design assets that could impair the own-IP verticalisation thesis (Surgery Connect / Evonex), but the issue is remediable via pre-close IP assignment deeds and registration, making it a standard closing condition rather than a deal-killer.
driver: Verticalisation / own-IP platform differentiation and re-rating thesis

title: General Conditions C2 / Cease Charges Regulatory Breach
rationale: A regulatory breach on cease charges creates a defined but containable liability and potential remediation cost that warrants a specific diligence condition but is unlikely to be material enough at this EV to threaten the 23% IRR base case absent evidence of a systemic, ongoing breach or a live enforcement action.
driver: M&A pipeline / regulatory compliance — could affect deal structure (price chip or escrow) but not thesis

title: Change-of-Control Termination Rights in Customer Contracts
rationale: CoC termination rights in customer contracts could elevate post-close churn above the ~7% base-case assumption, but the diversified, low-concentration customer book means even a modest uptick in triggered exits is unlikely to break the 23% IRR unless clustered in the high-margin Surgery Connect vertical, making this a condition/consent-solicitation diligence item rather than a deal-stopper.
driver: retention holding (churn assumption underpinning recurring revenue base)

title: Buyside CDD Phase I Only — Phase II Validation Absent
rationale: At 11.6x EBITDA and 6x opening leverage, Phase I CDD without Phase II validation leaves the IC without granular customer-level churn validation, NPS cohort analysis, and competitive win/loss data that underpin the retention and re-rating assumptions central to the 23% IRR; this is a real condition-to-close gap but not deal-changing because Phase I findings have not surfaced a thesis-breaking issue.
driver: retention holding / own-IP re-rating

title: CCaaS Scale Delivery Risk / Value Leakage to Vendors
rationale: CCaaS delivery dependency on third-party vendors creates margin leakage and execution risk on the verticalisation thesis (own-IP mix 30%→43%), but the finding does not threaten the existing SME base or near-term cash flows sufficiently to break the 23% IRR base case.
driver: Verticalisation / own-IP mix re-rating (Thesis Pillar 1 and 4)

title: Change of Control Triggers Mandatory Full Prepayment of Facilities
rationale: CoC prepayment obligations are a standard structural consideration that must be addressed as a closing condition (typically via lender consent, refinancing, or a new debt package), but at a £655m EV with 6x opening leverage already assumed in the model, this is an expected transactional mechanic that does not threaten the thesis or base-case returns if handled pre-close.
driver: none

title: NHS Deferred Income Unwind as Working Capital Driver
rationale: If NHS deferred income is inflating reported working capital or normalised cash conversion in the deal model, it could misstate the true cash EBITDA bridge and therefore the entry multiple, but it is a modelling/diligence correction rather than a thesis-breaker given Surgery Connect's structural position and recurring NHS demand.
driver: verticalisation / Surgery Connect cash EBITDA quality and leverage covenant headroom

title: Surgery Connect Ancillary Revenue CAGR Lacks Validation
rationale: Ancillary revenue growth within Surgery Connect is a named AI upsell return driver and contributes to the re-rating thesis, so unvalidated CAGR assumptions require a specific diligence condition but does not threaten the core Surgery Connect platform penetration or the broader SME/M&A thesis pillars underpinning base-case returns.
driver: AI ancillary upsell into Surgery Connect / own-IP mix re-rating

title: Legal DD Structural Limitations and Six-Month Staleness
rationale: Six-month-stale legal DD on a deal at 6x leverage with 50+ acquisitions in the structure creates real closing-risk and potential SPA warranty gap, requiring a refresh or bring-down confirmation as a condition to close, but does not itself threaten the thesis or base-case returns absent any specific adverse finding surfaced by that staleness.
driver: M&A / deal execution integrity; SPA / warranty risk management

title: M&A Pipeline Assumptions Without Individual Target Underwriting
rationale: M&A is a core thesis pillar and at 6x opening leverage any systematic overpayment or pipeline slippage could pressure returns, but the finding reflects an execution/diligence process gap rather than an identified failure in deal economics, and SCG's 50-acquisition track record provides a meaningful empirical base to stress-test aggregate assumptions.
driver: M&A continuation / inorganic EBITDA growth

title: NRR Trough at 94.4% FY24 / VDD Churn Granularity Not Disclosed
rationale: A 94.4% NRR trough in FY24 directly tests the retention-holding pillar of the base case, but without granular VDD churn data it is unquantified whether this is a secular deterioration or a one-period dip—requiring a diligence condition before close rather than being deal-changing, given the 7% headline churn figure and 35k+ customer base.
driver: Retention holding (thesis pillar 2) and IRR sensitivity to churn rate assumptions

title: Earn-Out Obligations Across Acquired Entities Proximate to Close
rationale: Earn-out obligations proximate to close create near-term cash leakage and potential balance-sheet liabilities that could pressure the already 6x levered structure, but are a known feature of an industrialised M&A model and manageable via standard W&I/SPA conditions and cash flow modelling rather than a deal-stopper.
driver: M&A engine / leverage headroom

title: Debtor Ageing Deterioration — Over-90-Day Balances Doubled
rationale: Doubling of over-90-day debtors is a meaningful working-capital and credit-quality signal that warrants verification, but at this stage it is a diligence condition rather than a thesis-breaker absent evidence of systemic churn or bad-debt provisioning shortfalls.
driver: Cash conversion / leverage serviceability

title: Horizon Margin Compression vs Operator Connect Economics
rationale: Operator Connect pricing dynamics could compress margins on the UCaaS/telephony stack over the hold period, but the shift toward own-IP platforms with ~55% GP share structurally mitigates this exposure as mix improves from 30% to 43%, making it a condition/monitoring item rather than a deal-breaker.
driver: Verticalisation / own-IP GP margin expansion underpinning re-rating

title: Vendor FDD Draft Status Unresolved / PwC Disclaims Accuracy
rationale: An unresolved PwC FDD draft with active accuracy disclaimers means the financial foundation underwriting the 11.6x entry multiple has not been formally signed off, creating a closing condition risk and potential for EBITDA adjustments — but absent specific identified misstatements it is a process/timing issue, not a deal-killer.
driver: M&A pipeline valuation accuracy / leverage structuring

title: Key Supplier Agreements Expired — Operating Informally
rationale: Expired supplier agreements create legal and commercial exposure that could disrupt the vendor-agnostic SME one-stop-shop model and M&A integration pipeline, but are typically curable via condition to close requiring counterparty renewals or comfort letters.
driver: Vendor-agnostic SME platform — supplier cost base and continuity underpinning reseller margin

title: X-On Health DPIAs Incomplete / Special-Category Health Data Exposure
rationale: Incomplete DPIAs on X-On Health (Surgery Connect) expose the business to ICO enforcement, fines up to 4% of global turnover, and reputational damage in the NHS/GP customer base, but this is a remediable compliance gap requiring a condition to close rather than a deal-killer given the business is operational and no breach has crystallised.
driver: Surgery Connect vertical — highest-GP-share platform and primary re-rating driver (30%→43% own-IP mix)

title: X-on Health Market Share Irreconcilable CDD Conflict
rationale: Conflicting CDD data on X-on Health / Surgery Connect market share creates uncertainty around the size and defensibility of the ~30% growth assumption, requiring reconciliation before close but does not by itself kill the deal given the product's demonstrated GP contribution and existing 55% gross profit share.
driver: Verticalisation / own-IP platform growth (Surgery Connect revenue trajectory and re-rating thesis)

title: Budget vs Actuals Revenue Shortfall / No Macro Contingency
rationale: A revenue shortfall versus budget signals execution risk and modest forecast credibility concern, but without evidence of structural churn deterioration or M&A pipeline collapse it does not break the base-case IRR on its own — it warrants a specific diligence condition requiring management to reconcile actuals-to-budget variance.
driver: retention holding / M&A revenue ramp assumptions underpinning 23% IRR base case

title: Overhead Cost Leverage Limited / People Cost FTE Jump
rationale: A structural inability to lever overheads as revenue scales would compress EBITDA margins and erode the re-rating multiple thesis, but the finding describes a cost trajectory issue rather than a deal-breaking flaw — it warrants a condition requiring management to present a credible headcount plan and revised margin bridge before close.
driver: Re-rating / margin expansion (own-IP mix growth and EBITDA conversion underpinning 11.6x entry multiple and 2.8x base case)

title: Recent Acquisitions Excluded from Datacube / ~9% GP Estimated
rationale: If ~9% of GP sits outside the Datacube, the industrialised M&A thesis pillar rests on an incomplete data foundation — churn, cohort, and retention metrics may be overstated or unvalidated for a material slice of the portfolio, requiring a condition to reconcile acquired-entity data into the model before close.
driver: M&A / retention metrics underpinning base-case GP and churn assumptions

title: Microsoft Teams Margin Dilution Risk / Cross-Sell Cannibalisation
rationale: Teams-native adoption could compress blended margins and cannibalise UCaaS/voice ARPU in the SME base, but SCG's Surgery Connect vertical is largely insulated (NHS/clinical workflow lock-in) and the SME book already operates at ~7% churn implying structural stickiness; the risk is real enough to require diligence but does not by itself break the base-case IRR.
driver: Verticalisation / own-IP mix re-rating and SME retention

title: Thesis Drift: Key Risk Disclosures Dropped Between Memo Revisions
rationale: Dropped risk disclosures between memo revisions is a process/governance red flag that warrants a condition requiring the IC to reconcile all prior drafts and confirm no substantive risks were deliberately suppressed, but absent evidence of a specific concealed material risk it does not itself break the return case.

title: Evonex Core Growth Materially Weaker Ex-Education Vertical
rationale: Evonex's ~30% growth narrative is a core re-rating driver, and if that growth is concentrated in one vertical (education) rather than broad-based, it raises execution risk on the thesis pillar around platform scalability, but does not by itself break the base-case IRR given Surgery Connect's 55% GP contribution remains intact.
driver: Evonex platform growth / own-IP mix re-rating pillar

title: Microsoft Teams SME Penetration Risk Not Stress-Tested
rationale: Teams/UCaaS commoditisation is a real structural headwind to the vendor-agnostic SME voice resale business but SCG's own-IP platforms are verticalised and sticky in ways Teams does not directly substitute, limiting the threat to a portion of the thesis rather than the whole; the absence of a stress-test warrants a specific diligence condition.
driver: retention holding / vendor-agnostic SME one-stop-shop pillar

title: Phone Mobile UK Entry (2026) and Direct Routing Growth Create Near-Term Competitive Disruption
rationale: New mobile/direct-routing entrants in 2026 could pressure SME churn above the ~7% base case and compress vendor margins, but SCG's Surgery Connect vertical lock-in and NHS/clinical workflow switching costs provide meaningful insulation that prevents this from being deal-changing.
driver: Retention holding (churn ~7%) and vendor-agnostic SME one-stop-shop margin

rationale: A near-doubling of customer count with materially lower revenue growth implies significant ARPU dilution, which could constrain the revenue and EBITDA uplift assumptions embedded in the M&A roll-up thesis and the upsell/cross-sell narrative, warranting diligence on unit economics and cohort revenue trends before close.
driver: M&A industrialisation / cross-sell upsell revenue growth

title: Director/Secretary Role Concentration in Wilson — Key Man Risk Amplifier
rationale: Wilson holding director/secretary roles across multiple group entities creates a structural key-man dependency that amplifies execution risk on M&A integration and Surgery Connect growth, warranting a condition around succession planning, but does not threaten the base-case returns on its own.
driver: backable management / M&A industrialisation

title: Verticalization Strategy Risks Not Quantified in IC Memos
rationale: The absence of quantified downside scenarios for the verticalisation thesis leg is a real diligence gap requiring explicit stress-testing of IRR sensitivity to slower vertical penetration before close, but the underlying business and cash flows are not themselves impaired by the memo omission.
driver: Verticalisation / own-IP mix re-rating (Thesis Pillar 1 & 4)

title: FTTP and SoGEA Margin Improvement Partly Driven by One-Off Wholesale Pricing Events
rationale: If a portion of the margin improvement embedded in the base-case EBITDA reflects non-recurring wholesale pricing events rather than structural unit economics, the normalised EBITDA may be overstated, requiring diligence to quantify the one-off benefit, but the own-IP verticalisation thesis remains intact.

rationale: Uncapped indemnities in major customer frameworks create contingent liability exposure that requires legal review and potential rep/warranty coverage at closing, but with 35k+ customers and no evidence of triggered claims, they do not threaten the retention thesis or base-case returns.

title: Vendor/Network Owner Value Chain Decline Not Quantified in Memo
rationale: Ongoing margin compression from wholesale price movements is a real but partially mitigated risk (own-IP mix growing 30%→43% is the explicit hedge); the memo's failure to quantify this headwind leaves the IC unable to stress-test how fast own-IP growth must occur to offset reseller margin erosion, making it a diligence condition.

rationale: A -34.1% gross margin on SIP calls is a real deterioration that warrants understanding of whether it is structural or transitional, but SIP calls is a legacy connectivity component rather than a core thesis pillar, making it a condition/diligence item requiring quantification rather than a deal-killer.

rationale: An FCA authorisation revocation on an acquired entity is a real regulatory flag requiring specific diligence on scope and successor liability, but absent evidence it affects core platforms or management fitness-and-propriety, it does not threaten the base-case thesis at this EV.

rationale: A legacy FSMA breach creates a real legal/regulatory tail risk requiring specific legal diligence and warranty/indemnity coverage at signing, but absent evidence of FCA investigation or systemic current non-compliance, it is unlikely to threaten base-case returns at this EV.

rationale: The trajectory of gross debt to £803.7m by FY34 warrants explicit IC disclosure and stress-testing of refinancing risk and covenant headroom, but does not by itself break the base-case return absent evidence of covenant breach or inability to service.

title: Mobile Segment Growth Assumptions Flagged as Ambitious by VDD
rationale: Ambitious mobile growth assumptions could pressure EBITDA and leverage covenants at 6x opening leverage, warranting a diligence reconciliation, but mobile is not a core thesis pillar so a shortfall is unlikely to break the 23% IRR on its own.

rationale: The Matrix Agreement governs a material wholesale or channel relationship whose mid-cycle renewal terms remain unconfirmed, creating uncertainty around cost structure that could affect EBITDA margins, but is resolvable as a closing condition once revised terms are confirmed.

rationale: A divergence between the P&L trading basis and statutory year-end adjustments creates uncertainty around the quality of reported EBITDA, requiring reconciliation before close, but is not inherently deal-changing if the adjustments prove routine.

rationale: If NHS Surgery Connect rollout overtime costs are running through reported EBITDA without normalisation, the LTM EBITDA base may be overstated, requiring a specific diligence adjustment confirmation before close rather than threatening the thesis outright.
